questions.question: Who among the following was NOT sentenced to death in the Kakori Conspiracy Case (1925)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sachindra Nath Bakshi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Kakori Conspiracy Case**, also known as the **Kakori Train Robbery**, took place on **9 August 1925**, in a small village called **Kakori** near **Lucknow**, **Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• **Rajendra Lahiri** was a prominent member of the **Hindustan Republican Association (HRA)**. He was found guilty of participating in the robbery and was awarded the **death sentence**. He was hanged in **Gonda Jail** on **17 December 1927**, two days before the scheduled date. *Statement 1 is incorrect as he was sentenced to death.*
 
• **Ashfaqulla Khan** was a key strategist and the first **Muslim** to be hanged in a conspiracy case against the **British Raj**. He was sentenced to a **death sentence** and was executed on **19 December 1927**, in **Faizabad Jail**. *Statement 2 is incorrect as he was sentenced to death.*
 
• **Sachindra Nath Bakshi** was a revolutionary and a member of the **HRA** who participated in the robbery. Unlike his comrades, he was **not sentenced to death**; instead, he was awarded **life imprisonment** (transportation for life) and sent to the **Cellular Jail** in the **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**. *Statement 3 is correct.*
 
• **Roshan Singh** (Thakur Roshan Singh) was another revolutionary involved in the conspiracy. Although he was not directly involved in the train robbery itself but was associated with the **Bamrauli action**, he was convicted and given a **death sentence**. He was hanged in **Naini Allahabad Jail** on **19 December 1927**. *Statement 4 is incorrect as he was sentenced to death.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hindustan Republican Association (HRA):**

 
 
• The **HRA** was a revolutionary organization established in **October 1924** in **Kanpur**.
 
• The founding members included **Sachindra Nath Sanyal**, **Ram Prasad Bismil**, and **Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee**.
 
• The **objective** of the association was to establish a **Federal Republic of United States of India** through an armed revolution.
 
• The **Kakori Train Robbery** was planned to acquire **funds** from the **British Treasury** to purchase weapons and support the organization's activities.
 
 
 
• **Ram Prasad Bismil:**
 
 
• He was the primary leader and mastermind behind the **Kakori robbery**.
 
• He was a gifted poet who wrote under the pen names **Bismil**, **Ram**, and **Agyat**.
 
• He was awarded the **death sentence** and hanged on **19 December 1927**, in **Gorakhpur Jail**.
 
 
 
• **Evolution to HSRA:**
 
 
• After the crackdown following the **Kakori** incident, the organization was reorganized as the **Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA)** in **1928** at **Feroz Shah Kotla, Delhi**.
 
• Leaders like **Chandrashekhar Azad**, **Bhagat Singh**, and **Sukhdev** played pivotal roles in this transition towards **Socialist** ideologies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Chandrashekhar Azad** was the only major leader involved in the **Kakori Conspiracy** who successfully **evaded arrest** by the **British police**. He continued the revolutionary struggle until his death in **Alfred Park**, **Allahabad** in **February 1931**.
 
• The **British Government** arrested approximately **40 revolutionaries** from various cities across **India** for their alleged involvement in the conspiracy.
 
• The legal defense for the revolutionaries was led by prominent figures such as **Govind Ballabh Pant** and **Chandra Bhanu Gupta**, although the **Special Magistrate's Court** ultimately handed down severe punishments to suppress the uprising.
 
• **Sachindra Nath Bakshi** survived his imprisonment and was released in **1937** after the formation of the **Congress** governments in provinces. He later participated in the **Quit India Movement** in **1942**.

questions.question: Who was popularly known as the ‘Lion of Punjab’ during the Extremist phase?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lala Lajpat Rai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lala Lajpat Rai** was a prominent Indian nationalist leader who played a pivotal role in the **Indian Independence Movement**. He was popularly known as **Punjab Kesari** or the **‘Lion of Punjab’** due to his fierce advocacy for self-rule.
 
• He was a key member of the **Extremist** faction of the **Indian National Congress**, famously known as the **Lal-Bal-Pal** trio, which included **Lala Lajpat Rai**, **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**, and **Bipin Chandra Pal**.
 
• In **1894**, he was instrumental in the founding of the **Punjab National Bank** (PNB), which was the first **Swadeshi** bank in India, and the **Lakshmi Insurance Company**.
 
• He led a non-violent protest against the **Simon Commission** in **Lahore** on **30 October 1928**. During this protest, he was severely injured in a **lathi charge** ordered by the local police superintendent, **James A. Scott**.
 
• Following the injuries sustained during the protest, he passed away on **17 November 1928**. His death sparked a wave of revolutionary activities among the youth of India, leading to the **Saunders' murder** case involving **Bhagat Singh** and his associates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bhagat Singh**:

 
 
• Commonly known as **Shaheed-e-Azam**, he was a charismatic Indian revolutionary who played a crucial role in the movement for independence.
 
• He founded the **Naujawan Bharat Sabha** in **March 1926** and was a leading member of the **Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA)**.
 
• He, along with **Batukeshwar Dutt**, threw non-lethal bombs into the **Central Legislative Assembly** in **April 1929** to protest against the **Public Safety Bill** and the **Trade Dispute Bill**.
 
• He was executed on **23 March 1931** at the age of **23** in **Lahore Jail**.
 
 
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**:
 
 
• Known as **Lokmanya** (accepted by the people) and the **'Father of Indian Unrest'** by British colonial authorities.
 
• He was a founding member of the **All India Home Rule League** established in **1916** alongside **Annie Besant**.
 
• He popularized the slogan, "**Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it!**" and published influential newspapers such as **Kesari** (in Marathi) and **The Mahratta** (in English).
 
 
 
• **Rajguru (Shivaram Hari Rajguru)**:
 
 
• A brave revolutionary from **Maharashtra**, he was a member of the **HSRA** and a close associate of **Bhagat Singh** and **Sukhdev**.
 
• He participated in the assassination of **John P. Saunders** in **1928** to avenge the death of **Lala Lajpat Rai**.
 
• He was hanged on **23 March 1931**, and his sacrifice is commemorated annually as **Shaheed Diwas** (Martyrs' Day).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Literary Contributions**: **Lala Lajpat Rai** was a prolific writer. His famous works include **'Unhappy India'**, **'The Political Future of India'**, and **'England’s Debt to India'**. He also founded the **Servants of the People Society** in **1921**.
 
• **Religious and Social Work**: He was deeply influenced by **Swami Dayananda Saraswati** and was a prominent leader of the **Arya Samaj** movement in **Punjab**.
 
• **Role in Congress**: He presided over the **Special Session** of the **Indian National Congress** in **Calcutta** in **1920**, where the **Non-Cooperation Movement** resolution was passed.
 
• **Legacy**: To honor his legacy, **Lala Lajpat Rai University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences** was established in **Hisar, Haryana**, and his birthday on **28 January** is celebrated in various parts of **India**.

questions.question: Article 23 specifically prohibits which practice?

options.text: Compulsory service in the armed forces

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Trafficking in human beings**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 23** of the **Constitution of India** is a significant provision that prohibits **trafficking in human beings**, **begar**, and other similar forms of **forced labour**.
 
• **Statement 1**: Compulsory service in the armed forces is not prohibited; rather, **Article 23(2)** allows the **State** to impose **compulsory service** for public purposes, such as military or social service, provided there is no **discrimination** based on **religion**, **race**, **caste**, or **class**. Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.
 
• **Statement 2**: The conferring of titles (except military and academic) is prohibited and regulated under **Article 18** of the **Indian Constitution** to ensure social **equality**. Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.
 
• **Statement 3**: The prohibition of **child employment** in factories, mines, or any **hazardous industries** is specifically covered under **Article 24** for children below the **age** of **14 years**. Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.
 
• **Statement 4**: **Trafficking in human beings** and **forced labour** are explicitly prohibited under **Article 23(1)**, and any violation is considered an **offence** punishable under the **law**. Hence, statement 4 is correct.
 
• The **Right Against Exploitation** is enshrined in **Articles 23** and **24** to protect the **dignity** of the individual and prevent exploitation by the **State** or **private persons**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Legislative Actions**: To implement the mandate of **Article 23**, the **Parliament of India** has enacted several **laws**, including the **Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956** and the **Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976**.
 
• **Scope of Article 23**: This **Fundamental Right** is available to both **citizens** and **foreigners**, and it acts as a safeguard against **exploitation** by both **State** authorities and **private individuals**.
 
• **Definition of Begar**: The term **'Begar'** specifically means involuntary **work** without **payment** or remuneration, which was traditionally practiced in **India** under the **zamindari system**.
 
• **Human Trafficking**: This involves the **illegal trade** of humans for **sexual slavery**, **forced labour**, or commercial **sexual exploitation**, which is strictly prohibited under the **Constitution**.
 
• **The 44th Amendment Act**: While **Fundamental Rights** can be suspended during an **Emergency**, the **Right Against Exploitation** remains a crucial pillar of **Indian democracy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 35**: Under this **Article**, the **Parliament** has the exclusive **power** to make **laws** to prescribe **punishment** for those acts declared as **offences** under **Article 23**.
 
• **Article 23(2) Exception**: The **State** can require **compulsory service** (like **conscription**) for **national security** or **social service**, but it cannot discriminate between citizens on **religious** or **racial** grounds while doing so.
 
• **Forced Labour**: The **Supreme Court of India** has interpreted **'forced labour'** broadly to include labor arising from **economic circumstances** where a person is forced to work for less than **minimum wages**.
 
• **International Context**: **Article 23** aligns with international standards like the **Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR)** and **International Labour Organization (ILO)** conventions against **forced labour**.

questions.question: The Digital India programme was launched in which year to enable digital delivery of services to citizens?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2015**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Digital India** programme was officially launched on **July 1, 2015**, by Prime Minister **Narendra Modi**. The initiative was designed to transform **India** into a **digitally empowered society** and a **knowledge economy**.
 
• It is an ambitious umbrella programme that covers multiple **Government Ministries** and **Departments**. It weaves together a large number of ideas and thoughts into a single, comprehensive vision so that each of them can be implemented as part of a larger goal.
 
• The **Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)** is the nodal agency responsible for the overall coordination and implementation of this flagship scheme.
 
• The motto of the programme is **"Power To Empower,"** focusing on three key vision areas: **Digital Infrastructure as a Core Utility to Every Citizen**, **Governance and Services on Demand**, and **Digital Empowerment of Citizens**.
 
• The programme aims to provide **high-speed internet** connectivity to all **Gram Panchayats** and ensure that government services are available to citizens **electronically**, thereby improving efficiency and transparency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The **Digital India** initiative is centered on **9 Pillars** of growth, which include:

 
 
• **Broadband Highways**: To cover all **2.5 lakh Gram Panchayats** under the **National Optical Fibre Network (NOFN)**.
 
• **Universal Access to Mobile Connectivity**: To ensure mobile coverage in the remaining **uncovered villages** in the country.
 
• **Public Internet Access Programme**: Strengthening **Common Service Centres (CSCs)** and transforming post offices into multi-service centers.
 
• **e-Governance**: Reforming government through **technology** by simplifying forms and tracking applications online.
 
• **e-Kranti**: Electronic delivery of services such as **e-Education**, **e-Healthcare**, and **e-Justice**.
 
• **Information for All**: Hosting data on **Open Data platforms** to facilitate transparency and accessibility for the public.
 
• **Electronics Manufacturing**: Aiming for **Net Zero Imports** in electronics by the **year 2020** through domestic production.
 
• **IT for Jobs**: Training youth in smaller towns and villages for **IT sector** jobs and **BPO** operations.
 
• **Early Harvest Programmes**: Implementation of quick-result projects like **Biometric Attendance** and **Wi-Fi in All Universities**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **DigiLocker**: A key initiative under the programme launched in **2015** to provide a secure **cloud-based platform** for storage, sharing, and verification of documents and certificates.
 
• **BHIM (Bharat Interface for Money)**: Launched in **December 2016**, it is a mobile payment app based on **Unified Payments Interface (UPI)** that facilitated the **digital payment** revolution in **India**.
 
• **UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance)**: A single mobile app that provides access to over **1,200 central and state government services**, supporting the goal of **mobile governance**.
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Gramin Digital Saksharta Abhiyan (PMGDISHA)**: One of the world's largest **digital literacy** programmes, aimed at making **6 crore rural households** digitally literate.
 
• **Impact and Data**: As of recent reports, **India** has seen a massive surge in **internet subscribers**, exceeding **800 million**, and has become the global leader in **real-time digital transactions**, accounting for nearly **46%** of global digital payments in **2022**.

questions.question: The National Small Industries Corporation was established in India in _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1955**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC)** was established in the year **1955** as a **Government of India** enterprise. ***Hence, the year 1955 is the correct answer.***
 
• It functions under the administrative control of the **Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME)**. It was created to promote, aid, and foster the growth of small industries in the country.
 
• In **1955**, the corporation started with the primary objective of facilitating the procurement of **government orders** for small-scale units and providing them with **machinery on a hire-purchase basis**.
 
• The **NSIC** acts as a nodal agency to implement various schemes of the **Ministry of MSME**, focusing on **Marketing**, **Technology**, and **Finance** support services for small enterprises.
 
• The establishment of **NSIC** in **1955** marked a significant step in India's industrial policy to encourage **entrepreneurship** and **employment generation** through the small-scale sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Marketing Support**: **NSIC** helps **MSMEs** through the **Single Point Registration Scheme (SPRS)**, which allows small units to participate in **Government Stores Purchase Programmes** without paying earnest money deposits.
 
• **Financial Assistance**: It provides **Raw Material Assistance** by financing the purchase of raw materials (both indigenous and imported) and also has tie-ups with **commercial banks** to facilitate working capital for small units.
 
• **Technology Support**: The corporation manages several **NSIC Technical Services Centres (NTSCs)** across **India** (e.g., in **New Delhi, Rajkot, Ludhiana, and Howrah**) to provide technical training and common facility support.
 
• **Exhibition and Trade Fairs**: To provide international and domestic exposure, **NSIC** organizes and participates in various **Trade Fairs** and **Exhibitions**, helping **MSMEs** showcase their products to a global audience.
 
• **B2B Portal**: **NSIC** manages a specialized **B2B Web Portal** (MSMEMart) to facilitate e-commerce and marketing linkages for small-scale industries in the digital era.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Headquarters**: The **NSIC** is headquartered in **Okhla, New Delhi**.
 
• **Mini Ratna Status**: The corporation has been recognized with the **Mini Ratna Category-II** status, reflecting its financial performance and operational efficiency as a **Public Sector Undertaking (PSU)**.
 
• **International Cooperation**: **NSIC** has shared the Indian experience of **Small Business Development** with many **developing nations** in **Africa** and **Asia**, helping them set up similar institutional frameworks.
 
• **ISO Certification**: It is an **ISO 9001:2015** certified company, ensuring that its service delivery and management systems meet **international standards**.
 
• **Other Options Context**: While **1954** saw the establishment of the **Small Industries Development Organization (SIDO)**, **NSIC** was specifically incorporated in **1955**. **1982** is notable for the establishment of **NABARD** and **EXIM Bank**, and **1975** marked the beginning of **Regional Rural Banks (RRBs)**.

questions.question: A solid cylinder is cut into 5 identical pieces by making cuts parallel to its flat surfaces. The curved surface area of all pieces is equal to the flat surface area of all pieces. If the total surface area of a piece is S square units, then the total surface area of the cylinder was ____ square units initially.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ Let original CSA = 2πrh and TSA = 2πrh + 2πr²

⇒ After cutting into 5 parts → CSA unchanged, flat surfaces increase

⇒ Given: total CSA = total flat area ⇒ 2πrh = 10πr²

⇒ ⇒ h = 5r

⇒ Each piece TSA = S = (2πr·h/5 + 2πr²) = (2πr² + 2πr²) = 4πr²

⇒ Original TSA = 2πr·5r + 2πr² = 12πr² = 3S

**∴ Answer = 3S**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cylinder cut into 5 equal parts

CSA (all pieces) = Flat surface area (all pieces)

**Formula:**

CSA = 2πrh

Flat area after cut = top + bottom + cuts = 2πr² + 8πr² = 10πr²

 
• 
• 
• 
•

• 

**Calculation:**

⇒ 2πrh = 10πr²

⇒ h = 5r

⇒ TSA of one piece = curved + top + bottom

⇒ = 2πr(h/5) + 2πr²

⇒ = 2πr(r) + 2πr² = 4πr² = S

⇒ Original TSA = 2πrh + 2πr²

⇒ = 2πr(5r) + 2πr² = 12πr²

⇒ = 3S

**Final Answer: 3S**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

questions.question: How many coins, each 5.5 cm in circumference and 2 mm thick, must be melted to form a cuboid of dimensions 14 cm × 11 cm × 8 cm? (Use π = 22/7)

⇒ Thickness = 2 mm = 0.2 cm

⇒ Volume of coin = πr²h = (22/7)×(0.875)²×0.2 ≈ 0.48125 cm³

⇒ Volume of cuboid = 14×11×8 = 1232 cm³

⇒ Number = 1232 / 0.48125 ≈ 2560

**∴ Answer = 2560**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Cuboid dimensions = 14, 11, 8 cm

⇒ 2πr = 5.5 ⇒ r = (5.5×7)/(44) = 0.875 cm

⇒ Volume of cuboid = 14×11×8 = 1232 cm³

questions.question: Three positive integers, a, b, c, satisfy: gcd (a, b) = 8, gcd (b, c) = 12, gcd (c, a) = 4 and LCM (a, b, c) = 240. Then, the minimum value of a + b + c is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Prime factorize LCM 240 = 2⁴ × 3¹ × 5¹.

Exponents for 2: gcd(a,b)=2³, gcd(b,c)=2², gcd(c,a)=2², LCM=2⁴ → powers are {4, 3, 2}.

Exponents for 3: gcd(b,c)=3¹, gcd(a,b)=3⁰, gcd(c,a)=3⁰, LCM=3¹ → a has 3⁰, b and c have 3¹.

Exponents for 5: Only one number can have 5¹ (as all gcd pairs lack 5).

Test case 1: a = 2³×5, b = 2⁴×3, c = 2²×3 → 40 + 48 + 12 = 100.

Test case 2: a = 2⁴, b = 2³×3, c = 2²×3×5 → 16 + 24 + 60 = 100.

**∴ Answer = 100**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

gcd(a, b) = 8, gcd(b, c) = 12, gcd(c, a) = 4, LCM(a, b, c) = 240

**Formula used:**

gcd(x, y) = Product of common prime factors with lowest powers.

LCM(x, y, z) = Product of all prime factors with highest powers.

 a=40 b=48 c=12 
• gcd=8 
• gcd=4 
• gcd=12 LCM (a, b, c) = 240 Min Sum = 40+48+12 = 100 

**Calculations:**

Let a = 2a¹ × 3a² × 5a³, b = 2b¹ × 3b² × 5b³, c = 2c¹ × 3c² × 5c³.

⇒ For prime 2: min(a1, b1)=3, min(b1, c1)=2, min(c1, a1)=2, max(a1, b1, c1)=4. This gives c1=2 and {a1, b1}={3, 4}.

⇒ For prime 3: min(a2, b2)=0, min(b2, c2)=1, min(c2, a2)=0, max(a2, b2, c2)=1. This gives a2=0, b2=1, c2=1.

⇒ For prime 5: min(a3,b3)=0, min(b3,c3)=0, min(c3,a3)=0, max(a3,b3,c3)=1. One of them is 1, others 0.

⇒ Case 1 (a3=1): a = 2³×5=40, b = 2⁴×3=48, c = 2²×3=12. Sum = 40+48+12 = 100.

⇒ Case 2 (c3=1): a = 2⁴=16, b = 2³×3=24, c = 2²×3×5=60. Sum = 16+24+60 = 100.

**∴ The correct answer is 100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM and GCD Property

For two numbers x and y, LCM(x, y) × GCD(x, y) = x × y. This does not directly apply to three numbers.

Prime Exponent Rule

The exponent of a prime p in GCD is the minimum of its exponents in the numbers, while in LCM, it is the maximum.

Coprime Numbers

If gcd(a, b) = 1, then a and b are called coprime or relatively prime numbers.

__
 
• The **Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Unnat Gram Abhiyaan (PMJUGA)** was launched in **2024**. It was initially announced by the **Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman** during the **Union Budget 2024-25** presentation. ***Hence, the statement regarding 2024 is correct.***
 
• The **Union Cabinet**, chaired by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, formally approved the mission on **September 18, 2024**, with a total outlay of **Rs. 79,156 crore**.
 
• This ambitious campaign is designed to improve the socio-economic condition of **tribal-majority villages** and **Scheduled Tribe (ST)** families across the country.
 
• The **Abhiyaan** aims to cover around **63,000 villages** in **549 districts** and **2,740 blocks** across **30 States and Union Territories**, benefiting approximately **5 crore tribal people**.
 
• It focuses on **25 interventions** implemented through **17 Central Ministries** to ensure **saturation** of government schemes in tribal areas.

• **Livelihood and Infrastructure:** Key focus areas include providing **pucca houses** under **PM Awas Yojana**, **piped water supply**, **electricity**, **all-weather roads**, and **high-speed internet** to remote tribal hamlets.
 
• **Sustainable Goals:** The mission aligns with the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)** by focusing on **health**, **quality education**, and **poverty reduction** specifically for the **indigenous communities** of **India**.
 
• **Tribal Health and Education:** It includes specific goals for **Sickle Cell Anaemia** screening and the strengthening of **Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS)** to boost **literacy rates** and **wellness** among tribal youth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

While **PM-JANMAN** focuses on **75 PVTGs**, the **PMJUGA** launched in **2024** has a much broader scope covering a larger **Scheduled Tribe** population.
 
• **Implementation Strategy:** The **Ministry of Tribal Affairs** acts as the **nodal ministry**, but the mission is a **convergence** of various schemes like **Jal Jeevan Mission**, **PMGSY**, and **Ayushman Bharat**.

questions.question: Which of the following Acts granted Delhi, the National Capital Territory, a legislative assembly?

options.text: Government of NCT of Delhi Act, 1991

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Government of NCT of Delhi Act, 1991**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi Act, 1991** was enacted by the **Parliament** to supplement the provisions of the **Constitution** relating to the **Legislative Assembly** and a **Council of Ministers** for the **National Capital Territory of Delhi**.
 
• This Act was passed following the **69th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1991**, which inserted **Article 239AA** and **Article 239AB** into the **Constitution of India**, providing a special status to the Union Territory of **Delhi**. ***Hence, the statement regarding the 1991 Act is correct.***
 
• The **Legislative Assembly** of **Delhi** was granted the power to make laws for the whole or any part of the **NCT** with respect to any of the matters enumerated in the **State List** or in the **Concurrent List**, except for three specific subjects: **Public Order**, **Police**, and **Land**.
 
• The Act specifies that the total number of seats in the **Legislative Assembly** shall be **70**, and these members are chosen by **direct election** from **territorial constituencies**.
 
• The **1991 Act** provides the operational framework for the functioning of the **Delhi Government**, including the conduct of business, the role of the **Speaker**, and the relationship between the **Lieutenant Governor** and the **Council of Ministers**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **69th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1991**: This amendment officially designated the Union Territory of **Delhi** as the **National Capital Territory of Delhi** and provided for a **Legislative Assembly** and a **Council of Ministers** headed by a **Chief Minister**.
 
• **Article 239AA**: This specific article describes the special provisions with respect to **Delhi**. It mandates that the **Administrator** of **Delhi** shall be designated as the **Lieutenant Governor (LG)**.
 
• **Delhi Administration Act, 1966**: Prior to the 1991 Act, **Delhi** was governed under the **Delhi Administration Act, 1966**, which provided for a **Metropolitan Council** and an **Executive Council**, but these bodies had limited recommendatory powers and were not a fully functional **Legislative Assembly**.
 
• **Comparison with other UTs**: Among the Union Territories in **India**, only **Delhi**, **Puducherry**, and **Jammu & Kashmir** (as per the **J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019**) are provided with their own **Legislative Assemblies**. **Puducherry** received its assembly through the **14th Amendment Act, 1962**.
 
• **Recent Amendments**: The **Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi (Amendment) Act, 2021**, and the **2023 Amendment** further clarified the powers of the **Lieutenant Governor**, stating that the expression "**Government**" referred to in any law made by the **Legislative Assembly** shall mean the **Lieutenant Governor**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Composition of the Council**: The **Council of Ministers** in **Delhi** is restricted to **10%** of the total number of members in the **Legislative Assembly**. Since there are **70 seats**, the **Council of Ministers** (including the **Chief Minister**) cannot exceed **7 members**.
 
• **Appointment**: The **Chief Minister** of **Delhi** is appointed by the **President of India** (not the **Lieutenant Governor**), and other **Ministers** are appointed by the **President** on the advice of the **Chief Minister**.
 
• **Year of Implementation**: While the Act was passed in **1991**, the first elections to the **70-member** **Delhi Legislative Assembly** were held in **1993**.
 
• **Responsibility**: The **Council of Ministers** is **collectively responsible** to the **Legislative Assembly** of the **National Capital Territory**.
 
• **Difference from States**: Unlike regular states where the **Governor** acts on the "**aid and advice**" of the ministers on most matters, in **Delhi**, the **Lieutenant Governor** has broader discretionary powers, particularly concerning matters outside the assembly's legislative competence (Police, Land, and Public Order).

questions.question: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST) was created by which Constitutional Amendment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**89th Amendment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **89th Amendment Act** of **2003** is the legislation that bifurcated the erstwhile combined **National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes** into two separate bodies. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• This amendment resulted in the creation of the **National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST)** under a newly inserted **Article 338A** of the **Constitution of India**.
 
• The **65th Amendment Act** of **1990** had previously replaced the single-member **Special Officer** for **Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes** with a multi-member high-level **National Commission**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The **97th Amendment Act** of **2011** is related to the constitutional status and protection of **co-operative societies**, adding **Part IXB** to the Constitution. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The **102nd Amendment Act** of **2018** granted constitutional status to the **National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC)** by inserting **Article 338B**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Evolution:** Originally, **Article 338** of the **Constitution** provided for a **Special Officer** (designated as the **Commissioner for SCs and STs**) to investigate all matters relating to the safeguards provided for them.
 
• **The 89th Amendment Rationale:** The separation was done to provide more focused attention on the **development** and **protection** of **Scheduled Tribes**, acknowledging that their geographical and cultural needs differ significantly from those of **Scheduled Castes**.
 
• **Establishment Date:** Following the **89th Amendment**, the **National Commission for Scheduled Tribes** officially came into existence on **19 February 2004**.
 
• **Constitutional Status:** As it is established directly by **Article 338A**, the **NCST** is a **Constitutional Body**, which gives it higher authority and autonomy compared to statutory bodies.
 
• **Geographical Focus:** The commission works across **India**, with specific focus on areas with high tribal populations, including the **Fifth Schedule** and **Sixth Schedule** areas mentioned in the **Constitution**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Composition of the Commission:** The **NCST** consists of a **Chairperson**, a **Vice-Chairperson**, and **three other members**. It is mandatory that at least one of the members is a **woman**.
 
• **Appointment and Tenure:** All members are appointed by the **President of India** by warrant under his hand and seal. Their **tenure** of office and conditions of service are determined by the **President**, usually fixed at **3 years**.
 
• **Powers:** The Commission has the power to regulate its own procedure and possesses all the powers of a **civil court** while investigating any matter. This includes **summoning** witnesses, requiring the **production of documents**, and receiving **evidence on affidavits**.
 
• **Functions:** Its primary duties include investigating and monitoring safeguards for **Scheduled Tribes**, inquiring into specific **complaints** regarding the deprivation of rights, and participating in the **planning process** of socio-economic development.
 
• **Reporting Mechanism:** The Commission submits **annual reports** to the **President**. The **President** causes these reports to be laid before each **House of Parliament** along with a memorandum explaining the action taken on the recommendations.

questions.question: What was the theme of the Emerging Science, Technology, and Innovation Conclave (ESTIC) held in November 2025?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Emerging Science, Technology, and Innovation Conclave (ESTIC)** held in **November 2025** adopted the theme **"Imagine, Innovate, Inspire for Viksit Bharat 2047"**. This theme reflects India's long-term vision of becoming a developed nation by the **100th year** of its independence.
 
• The conclave serves as a premier platform for **scientists**, **policymakers**, **industry leaders**, and **academia** to deliberate on the future of **Science, Technology, and Innovation (STI)** in India. The focus was on creating a roadmap that aligns scientific research with national economic goals.
 
• The **"Imagine"** component of the theme focuses on visionary thinking and foresight in disruptive technologies, while **"Innovate"** emphasizes the transition of ideas from laboratories to the market through **Research and Development (R&D)**.
 
• The **"Inspire"** element aims to cultivate a scientific temper among the **youth** and **start-up ecosystem**, ensuring a steady pipeline of talent to drive the **Viksit Bharat** agenda.
 
• During the event, various **National Missions** were reviewed to assess their progress toward making India a global hub for **manufacturing** and **technology** by **2047**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Viksit Bharat 2047:**

 
 
• This is a comprehensive vision by the **Government of India** to transform the country into a developed economy by **2047**. It involves key pillars such as **economic growth**, **social progress**, **environmental sustainability**, and **good governance**.
 
• In the context of science, it envisions India as a top **three global power** in **scientific publications** and **patent filings**.
 
 
 
• **Department of Science and Technology (DST):**
 
 
• Established in **May 1971**, the **DST** functions under the **Ministry of Science and Technology**. It is the nodal agency for organizing and promoting **science and technology** activities in India.
 
• It plays a critical role in funding **scientific research** and implementing high-end technology missions like the **National Quantum Mission**.
 
 
 
• **Key Technological Focus Areas:**
 
 
• The conclave highlighted several emerging fields such as **Artificial Intelligence (AI)**, **Quantum Computing**, **Semiconductor manufacturing**, and **Green Hydrogen**.

questions.question: Which leader was a close associate of Mahatma Gandhi and carried out a salt protest in the Madras Presidency during the Civil Disobedience Movement?

• **C. Rajagopalachari**, also known as **Rajaji**, was a prominent leader of the **Indian National Congress** and a close confidant of **Mahatma Gandhi**.
 
• During the **Civil Disobedience Movement** in **1930**, he was chosen to lead the salt protest in the **Madras Presidency**, mirroring **Gandhi’s Dandi March** in **Gujarat**.
 
• The protest, known as the **Vedaranyam Salt March**, commenced from **Trichinopoly** (now **Tiruchirappalli**) on **April 13, 1930**, and concluded at **Vedaranyam** in the **Tanjore district**.
 
• The march covered a total distance of approximately **150 miles** (**240 kilometers**) and lasted for about **15 days**, ending on **April 28, 1930**.
 
• By picking up salt at the **Vedaranyam** coast, **Rajaji** symbolically broke the **British Salt Laws**, leading to his subsequent **arrest** and **imprisonment** by the colonial authorities.

questions.question: Which of the following nuclear power stations has the highest capacity (Megawatt electric) as of 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kudankulam Atomic Power Plant**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Kudankulam Atomic Power Plant (KKNPP)**, located in the **Tirunelveli** district of **Tamil Nadu**, is the highest-capacity nuclear power station in India as of **2023**. It currently has an installed capacity of **2000 MW**, consisting of two **VVER-1000** units of **1000 MW** each. This makes it the leading contributor to India's nuclear energy grid. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• The **Tarapur Atomic Power Station (TAPS)** is located in **Palghar**, **Maharashtra**. It was the first commercial nuclear power station built in India, starting in **1969**. As of **2023**, its total capacity is **1400 MW**, comprising two older **160 MW** units and two newer **540 MW** units. While significant, its capacity is lower than Kudankulam. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• The **Kakrapar Atomic Power Station (KAPS)** is situated in **Gujarat**. With the recent commissioning of Unit 3 and Unit 4 (each **700 MW**), the total capacity has significantly increased. However, its total operational capacity as of early **2023** remained below the **2000 MW** mark set by Kudankulam. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The **Narora Atomic Power Plant (NAPS)** is located in the **Bulandshahr** district of **Uttar Pradesh**. It operates two **PHWR** units with a total capacity of **440 MW** (220 MW each). It has the lowest capacity among the four options provided. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL):**

 
 
• **NPCIL** is a **Public Sector Enterprise** under the **Department of Atomic Energy (DAE)**, Government of India. It was incorporated in **September 1987** under the **Companies Act, 1956**.
 
• Its primary objective is the design, construction, operation, and maintenance of atomic power stations for the generation of electricity in pursuance of the schemes and programs of the Government of India under the **Atomic Energy Act, 1962**.
 
 
 
• **International Cooperation in Nuclear Energy:**
 
 
• The **Kudankulam** project is a result of an inter-governmental agreement between **India** and the former **Soviet Union** (now **Russia**) signed in **1988**. **Russia** provides the technical expertise and **VVER** (Water-Water Energetic Reactor) technology.
 
• **Tarapur** was initially built with the help of the **United States** (General Electric), utilizing **Boiling Water Reactors (BWR)**, which were later supplemented by indigenous **Pressurized Heavy Water Reactors (PHWR)**.
 
 
 
• **India's Three-Stage Nuclear Power Programme:**
 
 
• Formulated by **Dr. Homi J. Bhabha** in the **1950s**, the program aims to utilize India's vast **Thorium** reserves.
 
• **Stage 1:** Uses **Pressurized Heavy Water Reactors (PHWR)** fueled by **Natural Uranium**.
 
• **Stage 2:** Uses **Fast Breeder Reactors (FBR)** fueled by **Plutonium-239**.
 
• **Stage 3:** Aims to use **Thorium-232** in **Advanced Heavy Water Reactors** to produce **Uranium-233**.
 
 
 
• **Geographic Distribution of Major Plants:**
 
 
• **Kaiga Generating Station:** Located in **Karnataka** with a capacity of **880 MW**.
 
• **Rajasthan Atomic Power Station (RAPS):** Located in **Rawatbhata**, **Rajasthan**, with a capacity of approximately **1180 MW**.

• **Clean Energy Contribution:** Nuclear energy is a critical part of India's strategy to achieve **Net Zero** emissions by **2070**, as it provides a stable "base load" of electricity without the carbon emissions associated with coal or gas.

All towels are cushions.

**Conclusions:**

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes the role of Self-Help Groups (SHGs) in India?

options.text: They provide large-scale industrial loans to farmers
They encourage thrift and extend micro-credit facilities to poor rural women
They operate as regional offices of the Reserve Bank of India
They function as government-owned cooperative banks

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They encourage thrift and extend micro-credit facilities to poor rural women**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Self-Help Groups (SHGs)** are informal associations of people who choose to come together to find ways to improve their living conditions. They are primarily designed to **encourage thrift** (savings) and provide **micro-credit** to their members. ***Hence, the statement that they encourage thrift and extend micro-credit facilities to poor rural women is correct.***
 
• These groups typically consist of **10 to 20 members**, mostly from similar **socio-economic backgrounds**, who pool their small savings regularly. This pooled resource is then used to give small **interest-bearing loans** to members for their emergency or consumption needs.
 
• **Statement 1** suggests they provide **large-scale industrial loans** to **farmers**. This is inaccurate as SHGs focus on **micro-finance** and small-scale livelihood activities rather than heavy industrial credit. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 3** claims they operate as **regional offices** of the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**. The **RBI** is India's **central bank** and a regulatory body; SHGs are community-based organizations and do not function as administrative arms of the **RBI**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 4** mentions they function as **government-owned cooperative banks**. While SHGs may link with banks, they are **self-governed** and **informal** in nature, unlike cooperative banks which are **statutory bodies** registered under the **Cooperative Societies Act**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Origin and Growth:** The SHG movement in **India** gained momentum in the **1980s**, pioneered by NGOs like **MYRADA** in **Karnataka**. It was formalized when **NABARD** (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) launched the **SHG-Bank Linkage Project** in **1992**, which has since become the world's largest **micro-finance** project.
 
• **Government Schemes:** The **National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM)**, renamed **Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana (DAY-NRLM)** in **2015**, is the flagship central scheme that promotes SHGs across **India** to alleviate **poverty** and promote **women's empowerment**.
 
• **Features and Functions:** SHGs work on the principle of **"Mutual Help"**. They help members overcome the lack of **collateral**, which is the biggest hurdle for the poor in obtaining **bank loans**. The **peer pressure** within the group ensures **timely repayment** of loans.
 
• **Social Impact:** Beyond finance, SHGs act as a platform for **rural women** to discuss social issues like **health**, **nutrition**, **domestic violence**, and **education**, leading to significant **social empowerment** and **gender equality** in **rural areas**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Economic Significance:** SHGs reduce the dependence of **rural households** on **informal moneylenders** who often charge **usurious interest rates**. By providing **affordable credit**, they enable **income-generating activities** such as **poultry**, **tailoring**, and **small-scale farming**.
 
• **Financial Inclusion:** They are a vital tool for **financial inclusion** in **India**, bringing the "unbanked" population into the **formal banking system**. The **SBLP (SHG-Bank Linkage Program)** allows groups to open **savings accounts** in **commercial banks**, **Regional Rural Banks (RRBs)**, and **cooperative banks**.
 
• **Membership Criteria:** Usually, only one person from a **family** can join a particular SHG. Most groups are **all-women groups**, as research shows that **credit** provided to **women** has a more positive impact on **family welfare** and **child education**.
 
• **Lakhpati Didi Initiative:** In recent years (specifically in **2023-2024**), the **Government of India** set a target to create **3 crore "Lakhpati Didis"** (SHG members earning at least **Rs. 1 lakh per annum**) through **skill development** and **market linkages**.

questions.question: At UNEA‑7, in December 2025, which initiative highlighted by India emphasizes individual and community action for environmental sustainability, contributing to SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption & Production) and SDG 13 (Climate Action)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mission LiFE**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mission LiFE** (Lifestyle for Environment) is an India-led global mass movement that encourages individual and community action to protect and preserve the environment. It was highlighted as a central theme by India at the **Seventh session of the United Nations Environment Assembly (UNEA-7)** held in **December 2025**.
 
• The initiative is designed to nudge individuals to adopt simple, environment-friendly actions in their daily lives, which collectively lead to a significant impact on **Climate Action** and **Sustainable Development**.
 
• It directly contributes to **SDG 12** (Responsible Consumption and Production) by promoting mindful utilization of resources and **SDG 13** (Climate Action) by reducing carbon footprints through sustainable lifestyle choices.
 
• The core philosophy of the mission is to replace the prevalent "use-and-dispose" economy with a **Circular Economy**, defined by mindful and deliberate utilization instead of mindless and destructive consumption.
 
• The mission envisions a global network of individuals known as **"Pro-Planet People" (P3)**, who share a common commitment to adopting and promoting environment-friendly lifestyles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Origin and Evolution**: **Mission LiFE** was first introduced by the Prime Minister of India during the **COP26** summit in **Glasgow** in **2021**. It was later formally launched at **Kevadia, Gujarat**, in **October 2022** in the presence of the **UN Secretary-General**.
 
• **Implementation Strategy**: The mission is implemented in three distinct phases:
 
 
• **Phase I (Change in Demand)**: Encouraging individuals to practice simple yet effective environment-friendly actions.
 
• **Phase II (Change in Supply)**: Inducing industries and markets to respond to the shift in demand by providing sustainable products.
 
• **Phase III (Change in Policy)**: Influencing government and industrial policy to support sustainable consumption and production.
 
 
 
• **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan**: Launched on **October 2, 2014**, this mission focuses on universal sanitation coverage and making India **Open Defecation Free (ODF)**. While related to the environment, its primary focus is hygiene and waste management rather than the broader lifestyle changes of Mission LiFE.
 
• **Make in India**: Launched in **September 2014**, this initiative aims to transform India into a global design and manufacturing hub. It focuses on **25 sectors** of the economy to create jobs and enhance skill sets.
 
• **Digital India**: Launched in **July 2015**, this campaign aims to ensure that government services are made available to citizens electronically by improving online infrastructure and increasing **Internet connectivity**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **United Nations Environment Assembly (UNEA)** is the world’s highest-level decision-making body on the environment. It meets **biennially** in **Nairobi, Kenya**, to set the global environmental agenda.
 
• The **UNEA-7** session in **2025** emphasized the "Triple Planetary Crisis": **Climate Change**, **Biodiversity Loss**, and **Pollution**.
 
• **NITI Aayog** is the nodal agency in India for coordinating the implementation of **Mission LiFE**, working alongside the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)**.
 
• Specific actions under Mission LiFE include **saving energy** (switching off lights), **saving water**, **reducing single-use plastic**, **sustainable food systems**, and **waste reduction** (e-waste and food waste).

questions.question: What are the different forms of a gene called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alleles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alleles** are defined as the alternative or different forms of a **gene** that occupy the same **locus** (position) on **homologous chromosomes**. They are responsible for the variations in a specific **hereditary characteristic**. ***Hence, the statement regarding Alleles is correct.***
 
• Every **individual** inherits **two alleles** for each **gene**, one from each **parent**. These alleles can be **identical** or **different**, determining the **genetic diversity** within a **species**.
 
• The **function** of alleles is to encode for slightly different versions of the same **protein**, which ultimately results in different **phenotypic traits** such as **eye color** or **blood type**.
 
• In **classical genetics**, alleles are categorized as **dominant** or **recessive**. A **dominant allele** masks the expression of a **recessive allele** in a **heterozygous** state.
 
• The **numerical value** of alleles for a single gene in a **diploid organism** is **2**, but in a **population**, there can be **multiple alleles** for a single trait.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Genotypes**: This term refers to the **complete genetic makeup** or **DNA sequence** of an **organism**. It is the internal **hereditary information** that contributes to the **physical expression** of traits. ***Hence, the statement regarding Genotypes is incorrect.***
 
• **Phenotypes**: This refers to the **observable physical characteristics** or **traits** of an organism, such as **height**, **skin color**, and **behavior**. It is the result of the **interaction** between the **genotype** and the **environment**. ***Hence, the statement regarding Phenotypes is incorrect.***
 
• **Chromosomes**: These are long, thread-like **structures** located in the **nucleus** of **animal** and **plant cells**. Each chromosome is made of **protein** and a single molecule of **deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA)**. Humans have **46 chromosomes** arranged in **23 pairs**. ***Hence, the statement regarding Chromosomes is incorrect.***
 
• **Gregor Mendel**: Often called the "**Father of Genetics**," he conducted experiments on **pea plants** in the **year 1865**, which led to the discovery of the **laws of inheritance** involving what we now call alleles.
 
• **Homozygous and Heterozygous**: When an individual has two **identical alleles** (e.g., **AA** or **aa**), they are **homozygous**; when they have two **different alleles** (e.g., **Aa**), they are **heterozygous**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Multiple Alleles**: While an individual carries only **two alleles**, a population can have **multiple alleles** for a gene. A **prime example** is the **ABO blood group system** in humans, which is controlled by **three alleles**: **IA**, **IB**, and **i**.
 
• **Incomplete Dominance**: This occurs when the **phenotype** of the **heterozygote** is an **intermediate** between the **phenotypes** of the two **homozygotes**. An **example** is the **pink flowers** produced by crossing **red** and **white** snapdragons.
 
• **Co-dominance**: In this **genetic scenario**, both alleles in a **heterozygote** are **fully expressed**. For **example**, in **AB blood type**, both the **A** and **B** antigens are present on the surface of **red blood cells**.
 
• **Mutation**: New alleles are created through **mutations**, which are **permanent changes** in the **DNA sequence**. This is a **key feature** of **evolution** and **biological adaptation**.

questions.question: Who among the following composed the work Rajashekharacharitra, which is a Prabandha dealing with the wars and loves of Rajashekhara, King of Avanti?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madayagari Mallana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Madayagari Mallana** was a distinguished **Telugu poet** of the **16th century** and a vital member of the **Ashtadiggajas**. This group comprised eight legendary poets who adorned the court of **Emperor Krishnadevaraya** during the **Vijayanagara Empire**.
 
• He is best known for composing the **Rajashekharacharitra**, a significant work in the **Prabandha** genre of **Telugu literature**. This literary piece intricately describes the life, **military expeditions (wars)**, and **romantic pursuits (loves)** of **Rajashekhara**, the **King of Avanti**. ***Hence, the statement regarding Madayagari Mallana as the author is correct.***

questions.question: The Harappan cities were famous for their ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Grid system of town planning**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Harappan Civilization**, also known as the **Indus Valley Civilization**, is world-renowned for its **advanced urban planning**. The most striking feature of these cities was the **Grid system**, where streets and lanes were laid out to cut each other at **right angles** (90 degrees), dividing the city into rectangular blocks.
 
• Unlike many contemporary civilizations, Harappan cities like **Mohenjo-daro** and **Harappa** were divided into two distinct parts: a raised **Citadel** (or Acropolis) on the western side, which housed important public buildings, and a larger **Lower Town** on the eastern side, where the common citizens resided.
 
• The use of **standardized burnt bricks** for construction was a hallmark of their engineering. These bricks followed a uniform ratio of **1:2:4** (thickness:width:length), ensuring structural integrity across various sites located hundreds of miles apart.
 
• Every house was connected to a highly **sophisticated drainage system**. These drains were made of mortar, lime, and gypsum and were covered with **stone slabs or large bricks** that could be removed for cleaning, indicating a high level of concern for **sanitation and hygiene**.
 
• The **Great Granaries** found at Harappa and Mohenjo-daro suggest a centralized system for storing surplus grains, which was a critical **economic feature** of their urban lifestyle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geographical Extent and Age**: The civilization flourished during the **Bronze Age**, roughly between **3300 BCE and 1300 BCE**, with its mature phase occurring between **2600 BCE and 1900 BCE**. It spread across present-day **India, Pakistan, and Afghanistan**.
 
• **Mohenjo-daro**: Located in the **Larkana district of Sindh, Pakistan**, on the banks of the **Indus River**. It is famous for the **Great Bath**, a large rectangular tank used for ritual bathing, and the discovery of the **Dancing Girl** bronze statue.
 
• **Harappa**: The first site to be excavated in **1921** by **Daya Ram Sahni**. It is located on the banks of the **Ravi River** in the **Sahiwal district of Punjab, Pakistan**.
 
• **Lothal**: Situated in **Gujarat, India**, this site featured the world's earliest known **artificial dockyard**, connecting the city to an old course of the **Sabarmati River**, facilitating maritime trade with **Mesopotamia**.
 
• **Dholavira**: Located in the **Rann of Kutch, Gujarat**, it is unique for its **three-part city division** (Citadel, Middle Town, and Lower Town) and an **extraordinary water management system** consisting of giant reservoirs.
 
• **Kalibangan**: Found in **Hanumangarh, Rajasthan**, it provides the earliest evidence of **ploughed fields** and contains both Pre-Harappan and Harappan cultural phases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Wooden houses**: While timber was used for roofs and doors, Harappan houses were primarily built with **baked bricks** and **mud bricks**. They did not rely on wooden structures as their primary architectural feature. **Hence, this statement is incorrect.**
 
• **Stone palaces**: The Harappans focused on **functional civic architecture** rather than monumental stone palaces or temples. While stone was used in sites like **Dholavira**, the concept of "stone palaces" as seen in later empires was absent. **Hence, this statement is incorrect.**
 
• **Irregular street patterns**: The Harappan cities were the antithesis of irregular patterns. They are celebrated specifically for their **planned, systematic layout** and geometric precision. **Hence, this statement is incorrect.**
 
• **Grid system of town planning**: This was the most defining characteristic of the Indus Valley Civilization, showcasing their expertise in **geometry and urban management**. **Hence, this statement is correct.**

questions.question: Which of the following pollutants is most closely associated with the formation of acid rain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sulphur dioxide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sulphur dioxide** (**SO2**) is a colorless gas with a pungent smell, primarily produced from the **burning of fossil fuels** like **coal** and **oil** in **power plants** and industrial boilers. It is the most significant pollutant closely linked to the formation of acid rain. ***Hence, option 2 is correct.***
 
• When **sulphur dioxide** is released into the **atmosphere**, it reacts with **water vapor**, **oxygen**, and other oxidants to form **sulphuric acid** (**H2SO4**), which then mixes with rain, snow, or fog.
 
• **Ammonia** (**NH3**) is a nitrogen-based compound often released from **agricultural activities** and **livestock waste**; while it can contribute to nitrogen deposition in soil, it is not the primary chemical driver for acid rain formation. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Ozone** (**O3**) is a **secondary pollutant** found in the **troposphere**, formed by the reaction of **Nitrogen Oxides** and **Volatile Organic Compounds** in the presence of **sunlight**. It is a major component of **smog** but does not directly cause acid rain. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Methane** (**CH4**) is a powerful **greenhouse gas** responsible for **global warming** and climate change, but it does not possess the chemical properties required to increase the acidity of precipitation. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Definition of Acid Rain:** It refers to any form of precipitation—rain, snow, fog, or hail—that is unusually **acidic**, meaning it possesses elevated levels of **hydrogen ions**. Normal rain has a **pH** of about **5.6**, whereas acid rain typically has a **pH** between **4.2 and 4.4**.
 
• **Nitrogen Oxides (NOx):** Along with **sulphur dioxide**, **nitrogen oxides** (emitted from **motor vehicles** and **electric utilities**) are the other major precursors. They react in the air to form **nitric acid** (**HNO3**).
 
• **Environmental Impact:** Acid rain causes the **acidification of lakes** and streams, which can be toxic to **fish** and other **aquatic animals**. It also leaches **aluminum** from the soil, which is harmful to **forest ecosystems** and **plants**.
 
• **Effect on Infrastructure:** It accelerates the **corrosion** of **metals** (such as **bronze**) and the **deterioration** of **paint** and **stone** (such as **marble** and **limestone**). Famous monuments like the **Taj Mahal** in **India** have faced threats of yellowing due to pollutants like **SO2** from nearby industries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Chemical Reaction:** The oxidation of **sulphur dioxide** to form **sulphuric acid** often occurs on the surface of **aerosol particles** or through liquid-phase reactions in **cloud droplets**.
 
• **Natural Sources:** While human activity is the leading cause, natural events like **volcanic eruptions** and **decaying vegetation** also release **sulphur dioxide** into the **atmosphere**.
 
• **Historical Context:** The phenomenon of acid rain was first observed by **Robert Angus Smith** in **1852** in **Manchester**, **England**, which was a hub during the **Industrial Revolution**.
 
• **Global Mitigation:** Many countries have signed **international treaties** and enacted laws like the **Clean Air Act** to reduce emissions of **SO2** and **NOx** through the use of **scrubbers** in power plants and **catalytic converters** in vehicles.

questions.question: The number of significant figures present in 0.00200 is ________.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **Pacific-Atlantic Rule** for significant figures:

1. If a decimal is **P**resent, count from the **P**acific (Left) side.

2. Skip all zeros until you hit the first non-zero digit.

3. Count every digit from that point until the end.

In $0.00\mathbf{200}$, we start counting at '2' and include the trailing zeros. Total = **3**.

**∴ Answer = 3**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Detailed Method__**

**Concept of Significant Figures:**

Significant figures represent the precision of a measurement. Every digit that is known with certainty plus one last digit that is somewhat uncertain is included.

**Rules Applied to 0.00200:**

• **Rule 1 (Leading Zeros):** Zeros to the left of the first non-zero digit (0.00) are never significant. They are simply placeholders to indicate the position of the decimal point.

• **Rule 2 (Non-zero Digits):** The digit '2' is non-zero, so it is significant.

• **Rule 3 (Trailing Zeros with Decimal):** Zeros at the end of a number are significant if a decimal point is present. These zeros ($...00$) indicate that the measurement was precise to that many decimal places.

0.00200
Leading Zeros (Placeholders)
 Significant Figures→ 3 Sig Figs

**Conclusion:**

Number = $0.00200$

Significant digits = $2, 0, 0$

Total count = $3$

**∴ The number of significant figures present in 0.00200 is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Scientific Notation Check

A foolproof way to find significant figures is to convert the number to scientific notation: $0.00200 = 2.00 \times 10^{-3}$. All digits in the coefficient part ($2.00$) are significant.

Significant Figures in Calculations

When multiplying or dividing, the result should have the same number of significant figures as the measurement with the *fewest* significant figures.

 Ratio Comparison Chart 3 : 17 0.176 13 : 67 0.194 10 : 37 0.270 5 : 9 0.555 (Max)

**Calculations:**

⇒ 3 ÷ 17 ≈ 0.1764

⇒ 13 ÷ 67 ≈ 0.1940

Same Difference Rule

In proper fractions, if the difference between numerator and denominator is the same, the fraction with the largest values is the greatest.

Reciprocal Method

If a/b is hard to calculate, compare b/a. The fraction with the smallest reciprocal value is the largest original fraction.

questions.question: What property do solids possess due to their closely packed particles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rigidity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rigidity** is the property of a substance to maintain its **shape** when an external force is applied. In **solids**, the constituent particles (atoms, ions, or molecules) are **closely packed**, leaving very little space between them. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Compressibility** refers to the capacity of a substance to decrease in volume under **pressure**. Because particles in a solid are already in **close proximity** and have **strong intermolecular forces**, they possess **negligible compressibility**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Transparency** is an optical property that allows light to pass through a material without being scattered. While some solids like **glass** are transparent, many others like **wood** or **iron** are **opaque**; therefore, it is not a property possessed by solids solely due to the packing of particles. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Fluidity** is the ability of a substance to flow, which is characteristic of **liquids** and **gases**. In solids, particles are held in **fixed positions** and can only **vibrate** about their mean positions, preventing them from flowing. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• The **strong intermolecular forces of attraction** in solids keep the particles so tightly bound that they exhibit a **definite shape** and **definite volume**, which are the fundamental aspects of **rigidity**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Solids**: Solids are characterized by **high density**, **low kinetic energy** of particles, and **incompressibility**. They do not expand to fill their container like gases do.
 
• **Crystalline Solids**: These solids have a **long-range order** with a regular repeating pattern of particles. Examples include **Diamond**, **Quartz**, and **Sodium Chloride**. They have **sharp melting points**.
 
• **Amorphous Solids**: Also known as **pseudo-solids** or **super-cooled liquids**, these lack a regular arrangement of particles. Examples include **Glass**, **Rubber**, and **Plastic**. They soften over a range of **temperatures**.
 
• **Density and Packing**: In a solid, the **packing efficiency** determines how much of the total space is occupied by particles. For instance, in a **Face-Centered Cubic (FCC)** structure, the packing efficiency is **74%**, which is quite high compared to other states.
 
• **Applications**: The **rigidity** of solids is utilized in **civil engineering** for **construction** (using steel and concrete), in **manufacturing** for creating durable **tools**, and in **aerospace** for structural components that must withstand high **mechanical stress**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Kinetic Molecular Theory**: According to this theory, the particles in a **solid** are in constant motion, but this motion is limited to **vibrations** because the **potential energy** of attraction is much greater than the **kinetic energy** of the particles.
 
• **Diffusion**: The process of **diffusion** (movement of particles from high to low concentration) is **extremely slow** in solids compared to liquids or gases because the **intermolecular spaces** are almost absent.
 
• **Thermal Expansion**: When a solid is heated, the **vibrations** of its particles increase, leading to a slight increase in volume known as **thermal expansion**. However, the **rigidity** remains until the **melting point** is reached.
 
• **Elasticity vs. Rigidity**: While **rigidity** is the resistance to change in shape, **elasticity** is the property of a solid to return to its original shape after the deforming **force** is removed (e.g., a **steel spring**).

questions.question: Which glacier, located in the Karakoram range, is the longest in this range and the second longest in the world outside the polar regions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Siachen Glacier**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Siachen Glacier** is located in the **Eastern Karakoram range** in the **Himalayan Mountains**, at approximately **35.42°N 77.10°E**.
 
• It is the **longest glacier** in the **Karakoram Range** and the **second-longest** in the world's **non-polar regions**, with a total **length** of about **76 kilometers** (**47 miles**).
 
• The only glacier longer than **Siachen** outside the polar regions is the **Fedchenko Glacier**, which is **77 kilometers** long and situated in the **Pamir Mountains** of **Tajikistan**.
 
• The **Siachen Glacier** lies just south of the great drainage divide that separates the **Eurasian Plate** from the **Indian subcontinent**.
 
• The **altitude** of the glacier ranges from approximately **5,753 meters** (**18,875 feet**) above sea level at its head at **Indira Col** to **3,620 meters** (**11,875 feet**) at its snout.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Baltoro Glacier**:

 
 
• Located in the **Gilgit-Baltistan** region of the **Karakoram range**.
 
• It has a **length** of **63 kilometers** (**39 miles**) and is one of the longest glaciers outside the polar regions.
 
• It is a **major source** of the **Shigar River**, which is a tributary of the **Indus River**.
 
• It is famous for its proximity to four of the world's fourteen "eight-thousanders," including **K2** (**8,611 meters**).
 
 
 
• **Gangotri Glacier**:
 
 
• Located in the **Uttarkashi District** of **Uttarakhand**, **India**, within the **Garhwal Himalayas**.
 
• It is one of the **largest glaciers** in the **Himalayas** with an estimated volume of over **27 cubic kilometers**.
 
• The glacier is about **30 kilometers** long and **2 to 4 kilometers** wide.
 
• The snout of the glacier is known as **Gaumukh**, which is the **source** of the **Bhagirathi River**, one of the main headstreams of the **Ganga**.
 
 
 
• **Pindari Glacier**:
 
 
• Situated in the **Kumaon** region of the **Himalayas** in the **Bageshwar district** of **Uttarakhand**.
 
• This glacier has a **length** of roughly **3.2 kilometers** and is the **source** of the **Pindar River**.
 
• It is a popular **trekking destination** in **India** due to its relatively easy accessibility compared to other Himalayan glaciers.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Siachen Glacier** is famously known as the **highest battlefield** in the world, where **India** and **Pakistan** have maintained a **military presence** since **1984**.
 
• In **April 1984**, the **Indian Army** launched **Operation Meghdoot**, a **military operation** to seize control of the glacier, which was successful.
 
• The **Nubra River** originates from the **snout** of the **Siachen Glacier** and flows into the **Shyok River**.
 
• Administratively, the entire **Siachen Glacier** is part of the **Union Territory of Ladakh** in **India** since the **reorganization** of the state in **October 2019**.
 
• The **Saltoro Ridge** serves as a **natural divide** that separates the **Siachen Glacier** from **Pakistan-occupied** territory.

questions.question: Under which section can we find the total processor utilization across all cores on a computer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Task Manager**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Task Manager** is a system monitor and startup manager utility included with **Microsoft Windows** systems that allows users to monitor **processor utilization**, **memory** usage, and **network** activity. ***Hence, the statement regarding Task Manager is correct.***
 
• To view the total processor utilization across all cores, a user must navigate to the **Performance tab** within the **Task Manager**. This section provides real-time **graphical data** on the **CPU (Central Processing Unit)**, showing the percentage of processing power currently being utilized.
 
• The utility allows users to see a single overall graph or right-click to change the view to "**Logical processors**," which displays the utilization of every **individual core** and **thread** in the system.
 
• It serves as a critical **diagnostic tool** for identifying **applications** or **background processes** that are consuming excessive resources, potentially slowing down the **computer**.
 
• The **Task Manager** can be quickly accessed by pressing the keyboard shortcut **Ctrl + Shift + Esc** or by right-clicking the **Taskbar** in most **Windows** versions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **My Computer (This PC):**

 
 
• This is a **system folder** and **file management** interface used to access drives like the **C: Drive**, **D: Drive**, and external storage devices.
 
• It provides information about **disk space** and **file hierarchy** but does not show real-time **CPU utilization**. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Settings:**
 
 
• This is a **universal app** in **Windows 10** and **Windows 11** designed to replace the legacy **Control Panel** for configuring **system preferences**.
 
• While it contains **"About"** information showing the **processor model** and **RAM capacity**, it is not the primary tool for monitoring **live utilization** across all cores. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Recycle Bin:**
 
 
• The **Recycle Bin** is a directory where **deleted files** are temporarily stored before being permanently removed from the **hard drive**.
 
• It has no function related to **hardware monitoring** or **system performance** tracking. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **History of Task Manager:** It was significantly overhauled in **Windows 8** and **Windows 10**, introducing a cleaner **"Processes"** tab that groups applications and background tasks separately for better **management**.
 
• **Metrics Tracked:** Beyond **CPU**, the **Performance tab** tracks **GPU (Graphics Processing Unit)** utilization, **Disk Read/Write speeds**, and **Ethernet/Wi-Fi** throughput.
 
• **Process Management:** If a **software program** becomes unresponsive, the **Task Manager** allows a user to **"End Task,"** which forcefully terminates the **process** to free up **system resources**.
 
• **Uptime:** The utility also displays the **System Uptime** (in **Days:Hours:Minutes:Seconds**), which indicates how long the **computer** has been running since the last **reboot** or **startup**.
