questions.question: The founder of the Chola empire, Vijayalaya, was the feudatory of which of the following South Indian powers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pallavas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vijayalaya** was the founder of the **Imperial Chola Empire** in **South India** during the **9th century**. He belonged to the ancient **Chola** family of **Uraiyur**, which had a glorious past during the **Sangam Age** but had later declined into a minor power.
 
• Before establishing an independent kingdom, **Vijayalaya** served as a **feudatory** (vassal) of the **Pallavas** of **Kanchipuram**. This relationship highlights the political structure of the era where smaller local chieftains owed allegiance to dominant regional powers like the **Pallavas**.
 
• Around the **year 850 AD**, **Vijayalaya** took advantage of the constant warfare between the **Pallavas** and the **Pandyas**. He defeated the **Muttharaiyars**, who were subordinates to the **Pandya** kings and controlled the **Kaveri delta**.
 
• After capturing **Thanjavur** from the **Muttharaiyars**, he established it as the **capital** of the rising **Chola** kingdom. He also constructed a magnificent temple dedicated to the goddess **Nishumbhasudini** (a form of **Durga**) in **Thanjavur** to commemorate his victory.
 
• His reign lasted from **850 AD** to **871 AD**, laying the essential groundwork for his successors, particularly **Aditya I**, to expand the empire and eventually overthrow their **Pallava** overlords.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pallava Dynasty**:

 
 
• The **Pallavas** ruled from **Kanchipuram** from the **3rd century** to the **9th century AD**.
 
• They were pioneers of **Dravidian architecture**, famously known for the **rock-cut temples** at **Mahabalipuram** and the **Shore Temple**.
 
• The **Pallava** power finally declined when the **Chola** ruler **Aditya I** defeated the last **Pallava** king, **Aparajita**, in **897 AD**.
 
 
 
• **Chalukya Dynasty**:
 
 
• The **Chalukyas** were a major power in the **Deccan** region, with their capital at **Badami** (Vatapi).
 
• **Pulakeshin II** (**610–642 AD**) was their most famous ruler, known for defeating **Harshavardhana** on the banks of the **Narmada River**.
 
• They were persistent rivals of the **Pallavas**, often engaging in long-drawn conflicts over the fertile **Raichur Doab**.
 
 
 
• **Western Ganga Dynasty**:
 
 
• The **Gangas** ruled the southern part of modern-day **Karnataka**, a region known as **Gangavadi**, from the **4th to the 10th century**.
 
• They often maintained their sovereignty by playing the role of a buffer state between the **Pallavas**, **Chalukyas**, and **Rashtrakutas**.
 
• They are well-known for the **monolithic statue** of **Lord Bahubali** (Gommateshwara) at **Shravanabelagola**, commissioned during the **10th century**.
 
 
 
• **Vakataka Dynasty**:
 
 
• The **Vakatakas** were a powerful dynasty in the **Deccan** (modern **Maharashtra** and **Madhya Pradesh**) from the **3rd to 5th century AD**.
 
• They were contemporaries of the **Guptas** and entered into matrimonial alliances with them (e.g., **Prabhavatigupta**).
 
• They were significant patrons of the **Ajanta Caves**, particularly during the reign of **Harisena**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Imperial Chola** dynasty established by **Vijayalaya** reached its zenith under **Rajaraja I** (**985–1014 AD**) and **Rajendra I** (**1014–1044 AD**).
 
• **Rajaraja I** constructed the world-famous **Brihadisvara Temple** in **Thanjavur** around **1010 AD**, which is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.
 
• The **Cholas** are celebrated for their highly efficient **local self-government** system, as evidenced by the **Uttaramerur Inscription**, and for their **maritime expeditions** to **Sri Lanka** and **Southeast Asia** (Srivijaya empire).
 
• The transition from a **Pallava feudatory** to an independent empire showcases the **Cholas'** strategic ability to exploit political vacuums in the **medieval South Indian** landscape.

questions.question: What is the maximum value that must be assigned to A so that the 8-digit number 230A7807 is divisible by 3?

questions.question: A quadratic polynomial f(x) gives a remainder of 5 when divided by (x - 2), and of -3 when divided by (x - 4). If f(x) is of the form ax² + bx + c and the leading coefficient is 1, then which of the following is the correct quadratic equation f(x)=0?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use Remainder Theorem:

⇒ f(2) = 5, f(4) = −3

⇒ Assume f(x) = x² + bx + c

⇒ Substitute: 4 + 2b + c = 5 and 16 + 4b + c = −3

⇒ Solve quickly ⇒ b = −10, c = 21

**∴ Answer: x² − 10x + 21 = 0**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

f(x) = x² + bx + c

f(2) = 5, f(4) = −3

**Concept Used:**

Remainder Theorem → f(a) gives remainder when divided by (x − a)

**Calculation:**

⇒ f(2) = 2² + 2b + c = 5

⇒ 4 + 2b + c = 5

⇒ 2b + c = 1 ...(1)

⇒ f(4) = 4² + 4b + c = −3

⇒ 16 + 4b + c = −3

⇒ 4b + c = −19 ...(2)

⇒ Subtract (1) from (2):

⇒ (4b + c) − (2b + c) = −19 − 1

⇒ 2b = −20 ⇒ b = −10

⇒ Put in (1):

⇒ 2(−10) + c = 1

⇒ −20 + c = 1 ⇒ c = 21

⇒ f(x) = x² − 10x + 21

**∴ Required equation: x² − 10x + 21 = 0**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Remainder Theorem:** f(a) = remainder when divided by (x − a)

**Quadratic Form:** ax² + bx + c

**Leading Coefficient:** Here a = 1 simplifies calculation

**Shortcut Tip:** Form equations directly using given values

questions.question: What contributed to the height of the Citadel in the Harappan civilisation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mud brick platforms**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Citadel** or the **Acropolis** was a distinct feature of the **Harappan civilisation**, typically located on the **western side** of the city. It was built on massive **mud brick platforms** to provide it with a significant elevation compared to the rest of the settlement. ***Hence, the statement regarding mud brick platforms is correct.***
 
• This architectural design served a dual purpose: it provided **protection against floods** from rivers like the **Indus** and acted as a **defensive fortification**. The height physically separated the administrative and ritual centers from the **Lower Town**.
 
• Most of the important public buildings, such as the **Great Bath** in **Mohenjo-daro** and various **Granaries**, were located on this elevated Citadel. The platforms were made of millions of **mud bricks**, requiring a massive amount of labor and organization.
 
• While **stone construction** was used in specific sites like **Dholavira** in **Gujarat**, it was not the primary factor for the height of Citadels across most Harappan cities. In most major sites, **mud bricks** were the fundamental material for the elevated bases. ***Hence, the statement regarding stone construction is generally incorrect for height contribution.***
 
• **Wooden pillars** were used for the superstructures or roofs of buildings but did not contribute to the foundational height of the Citadel itself. ***Hence, the statement regarding wooden pillars is incorrect.***
 
• **Adobe walls** (sun-dried bricks) were used for constructing the walls of houses and fortifications, but the actual **elevation** of the entire zone was due to the artificial **mud brick platforms**. ***Hence, the statement regarding adobe walls is not the primary reason for the height.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Town Planning:** The **Harappan Civilisation** (also known as the **Indus Valley Civilisation**), dating from approximately **2600 BCE to 1900 BCE**, is famous for its advanced **urban planning**. Cities were divided into the **Citadel** (for the elite/administration) and the **Lower Town** (for commoners and craftsmen).
 
• **Geographic Location:** The civilisation spanned across modern-day **India** (Punjab, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana) and **Pakistan** (Sindh, Punjab, Balochistan). Key sites include **Harappa**, **Mohenjo-daro**, **Kalibangan**, and **Lothal**.
 
• **Brick Standardization:** One of the most remarkable features was the use of **standardized bricks**. Whether **sun-dried (mud bricks)** or **baked (burnt bricks)**, they followed a strict ratio of **4:2:1** in terms of length, breadth, and height.
 
• **The Great Bath:** Located on the Citadel at **Mohenjo-daro**, this was a large rectangular tank used for **ritual bathing**. It was made watertight with a layer of **natural bitumen** (tar), showcasing advanced engineering skills.
 
• **Granaries:** Huge structures used for storing surplus **food grains** like **wheat** and **barley** were found on the Citadels, indicating a centralized tax or grain collection system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Social Stratification:** The physical elevation of the Citadel on **mud brick platforms** suggests a clear **social hierarchy**, where the ruling class lived apart from the general population.
 
• **Labor Organization:** The construction of these platforms involved **millions of man-hours**. Archaeologists estimate that to build the platforms at **Harappa** alone, thousands of laborers would have worked for months, implying a powerful **centralized authority**.
 
• **Drainage System:** While the Citadel was raised, the **Lower Town** featured the world's first sophisticated **underground drainage system**. Every house was connected to street drains lined with **bricks** or **stone slabs**.
 
• **Discovery:** The first Harappan site was discovered in **1921** by **Daya Ram Sahni** under the guidance of **Sir John Marshall**. **Mohenjo-daro** was subsequently excavated by **R.D. Banerji** in **1922**.
 
• **Decline:** The civilization began to decline around **1900 BCE** due to various factors including **climate change**, **flooding**, or the drying up of the **Saraswati River**.

questions.question: Ansh walks to his school at a certain speed from his home in the morning and returns in the afternoon at a speed, which is 2 km/h slower than his speed in the morning. If the average speed of Ansh of going to and coming back from the school is 4.8 km/h, find the sum of the speeds (in km/h) of Ansh in the morning and afternoon.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ Let speeds be v and v−2

⇒ Average speed = (2×v(v−2)) / (2v−2) = 4.8

⇒ Try nearby values → v = 6 works

⇒ Speeds = 6 and 4

**∴ Answer = 10**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Morning speed = v

Afternoon speed = v − 2

Average speed = 4.8 km/h

**Formula:**

Average speed (equal distance) = (2ab)/(a + b)

**Calculation:**

⇒ 4.8 = (2 × v × (v − 2)) / (v + v − 2)

⇒ 4.8 = (2v(v − 2)) / (2v − 2)

⇒ 4.8(2v − 2) = 2v(v − 2)

⇒ 9.6v − 9.6 = 2v² − 4v

⇒ 2v² − 13.6v + 9.6 = 0

⇒ Divide by 2 ⇒ v² − 6.8v + 4.8 = 0

⇒ v = 6 (valid)

⇒ Speeds = 6 and 4

⇒ Sum = 6 + 4 = 10

**Final Answer: 10**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

questions.question: Which forest type in India is known for its year-round green canopy due to no fixed period of leaf shedding?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tropical evergreen forests**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tropical evergreen forests** are found in regions receiving heavy **rainfall** of more than **200 cm** with a short dry season. Because of the high heat and humidity, these forests do not have a specific time to shed their leaves, making them appear green all year round. *Hence, this option is correct.*
 
• These forests are highly **stratified**, meaning they have layers of vegetation starting from **shrubs** and **creepers** at the bottom to tall trees reaching heights of **60 meters** or above.
 
• In **India**, these forests are predominantly located on the western slopes of the **Western Ghats**, the island groups of **Lakshadweep**, **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**, and the upper parts of **Assam** and the **Tamil Nadu** coast.
 
• The **flora** of these forests include commercially important trees such as **Ebony**, **Mahogany**, **Rosewood**, **Rubber**, and **Cinchona**.
 
• Common **fauna** found in these regions include **elephants**, **monkeys**, **lemurs**, and **deer**, while the jungles of **Assam** and **West Bengal** are famous for the **one-horned rhinoceros**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tropical Thorn Forests**:

 
 
• These are found in regions with less than **70 cm** of **rainfall**. The vegetation consists of thorny trees and bushes like **Acacias**, **Palms**, **Euphorbias**, and **Cacti**.
 
• They are common in the semi-arid areas of **Northwest India**, including **Gujarat**, **Rajasthan**, **Madhya Pradesh**, and **Haryana**. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
 
 
• **Dry Deciduous Forests**:

This includes adding more **RAM**, **Graphics Cards**, or **external storage** via **USB** or **PCIe slots**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Flexibility**, often called **versatility**, describes the computer's capability to perform **completely different types of work**. For example, the same machine can be used to **write a document**, **play music**, **edit video**, or **manage a database**. While it makes the machine **multi-purpose**, it is not the term for ensuring identical outputs for identical inputs. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

• **Accuracy**: In addition to being fast, computers are extremely **accurate**. The **degree of accuracy** depends on the **design** of the computer. If the **programming** and **input** are correct, the **results** will be 100% accurate. Most errors are **human-driven** rather than **machine-driven**.
 
• **Storage Capacity**: Computers can store **vast amounts of data** in very small physical spaces. **Primary storage** (like **RAM**) holds data currently in use, while **Secondary storage** (like **Hard Disk Drives**, **Solid State Drives**, and **Optical Discs**) can store **terabytes** of information for **long-term use**.
 
• **Diligence**: Unlike **human beings**, a computer is free from **monotony**, **tiredness**, and **lack of concentration**. It can work for **24 hours** a day, **365 days** a year without any decrease in **performance** or **precision**.

questions.question: Which of the following rulers of the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty is credited with resisting Arab invasions effectively?

• **Nagabhata I** established his control over **Ujjain** and laid the foundation for a dynasty that would eventually dominate **Northern India** for over **three centuries**.
 
• In contrast, **Ramabhadra** (reign **833–836 CE**) was a relatively weak ruler who could not maintain the vast empire inherited from **Nagabhata II**, leading to temporary territorial losses. ***Hence, the statement regarding Ramabhadra is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• He was the most powerful and celebrated ruler of the **Gurjara-Pratihara** dynasty. Under his leadership, the empire reached its **zenith**, stretching from the **Sutlej River** in the northwest to the **Narmada River** in the south.
 
• He was a devotee of **Lord Vishnu** and adopted the title **Adivaraha**, which is found inscribed on his **silver coins**.
 
• The **Arab** traveler **Al-Masudi** referred to the **Pratihara** king as **Baura** (a corruption of **Adivaraha**), noting his great military strength and hostility toward the **Arabs**.

While he also fought against **Arab** incursions and forged an alliance with **Lalitaditya Muktapida** of **Kashmir**, he belonged to a different lineage and was eventually defeated by **Lalitaditya**.
 
 
 
• **Tripartite Struggle:**
 
 
• The **Gurjara-Pratiharas** were constantly involved in the **Tripartite Struggle** for the control of **Kannauj**.
 
• This struggle involved three major powers: the **Pratiharas** of the west, the **Palas** of **Bengal**, and the **Rashtrakutas** of the **Deccan**.
 
• The **Pratiharas** eventually emerged as the dominant force in **Kannauj** during the reign of **Nagabhata II** in **816 CE**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Art and Architecture:** They were great patrons of **temple architecture**. Notable examples include the **Teli ka Mandir** in **Gwalior Fort** and the temples at **Osian** in **Rajasthan**. Their style is characterized by **elaborate carvings** and the **Nagara** school of architecture.
 
• **Literature:** The famous poet and dramatist **Rajasekhara** lived in the court of **Mahendrapala I** and **Mahipala I**. He authored works like **Karpuramanjari**, **Kavyamimamsa**, and **Balabharata**.
 
• **Decline:** The dynasty began to decline in the **10th century** due to repeated invasions by the **Rashtrakuta** king **Indra III** and later by **Mahmud of Ghazni** in **1018 CE**, which eventually led to the rise of smaller **Rajput** clans like the **Chandelas** and **Chahamanas**.

questions.question: In which year was the 52nd Amendment Act of the Indian Constitution, which introduced the Anti‑Defection Law to prevent elected representatives from switching political parties, passed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1985**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **52nd Amendment Act** was passed by the **Parliament of India** in the year **1985** to address the issue of political defections. *Hence, the statement regarding **1985** is correct.*
 
• The act introduced what is popularly known as the **Anti-Defection Law**, which was designed to provide stability to the **government** by preventing **elected representatives** (MPs and MLAs) from changing parties frequently for personal or political gain.
 
• Through this amendment, the **Tenth Schedule** was added to the **Constitution of India**, detailing the grounds and process for disqualification of legislators.
 
• The amendment amended **Articles 101, 102, 190, and 191** of the Constitution to include provisions related to vacation of seats and disqualification on the grounds of defection.
 
• The primary objective was to curb the "**Aaya Ram Gaya Ram**" culture in Indian politics, which refers to the frequent floor-crossing by **legislators** that often led to the collapse of stable governments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Provisions for Disqualification:** A member of a **House** belonging to any **political party** becomes disqualified if they voluntarily give up their membership or vote (or abstain from voting) contrary to the directions issued by their party (the **Whip**) without prior permission.
 
• **Independent and Nominated Members:** An **independent member** becomes disqualified if they join any political party after the **election**. A **nominated member** is disqualified if they join a political party after **six months** from the date they take their seat.
 
• **The 91st Amendment Act, 2003:** This amendment strengthened the **Anti-Defection Law** by removing the provision that protected a "**split**" (where **one-third** of members left). Now, at least **two-thirds** of the members of a party must agree to a "**merger**" with another party to avoid disqualification.
 
• **Role of the Presiding Officer:** The decision on disqualification is taken by the **Speaker** (in the **Lok Sabha** or **Legislative Assembly**) or the **Chairman** (in the **Rajya Sabha** or **Legislative Council**). Their decision was initially final, but the **Supreme Court** in the **Kihoto Hollohan case (1992)** ruled that the decision is subject to **judicial review**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **1990 (Option 1):** This year is significant in the history of electoral reforms as the **Dinesh Goswami Committee** submitted its report on **Electoral Reforms**, which suggested changes to the **Anti-Defection Law**, but it is not the year the **52nd Amendment** was passed. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
• **1975 (Option 2):** This year is known for the imposition of the **National Emergency** by **Indira Gandhi**. Several major amendments like the **38th** and **39th Amendment Acts** were passed in **1975**, but the **Anti-Defection Law** did not exist then. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
• **1980 (Option 3):** In **1980**, the **Supreme Court** delivered its landmark judgment in the **Minerva Mills case**, which strengthened the **Basic Structure Doctrine** of the **Constitution**. However, no **Anti-Defection** legislation was enacted in this **year**. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
• **Numerical Fact:** Under the **91st Amendment (2003)**, the total number of **ministers**, including the **Prime Minister**, in the **Council of Ministers** shall not exceed **15%** of the total strength of the **Lok Sabha**.

questions.question: Which city hosted the signing of the first universal legal framework to combat the escalating threat of cybercrime worldwide, when 72 nations signed the United Nations Convention against Cybercrime?

__
 
• **Hanoi, Vietnam**, hosted the signing of the first UN Convention against Cybercrime on October 25-26, 2025, where 72 nations signed the treaty.
 
• This historic event aimed to establish a universal legal framework to combat rising global digital threats, with the treaty officially nicknamed the "Hanoi Convention".
 
• This convention represents the **first global legally binding instrument** designed to address the escalating threat of cybercrime. It was drafted by an **Ad Hoc Committee** established by the **UN General Assembly**. ***Hence, the statement regarding the framework being universal and legal is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

The **Ad Hoc Committee** was tasked with elaborating a comprehensive international convention on countering the use of **ICTs (Information and Communications Technologies)** for criminal purposes.
 
• **Comparison with Budapest Convention:** Prior to this UN treaty, the **Budapest Convention (2001)**, initiated by the **Council of Europe**, was the primary international treaty. However, it was not **universal** as many nations, including **India**, **Russia**, and **China**, were not parties to it due to concerns over **sovereignty** and **data access**.
 
• **Scope of Crimes:** The new **UN Convention** covers a wide array of offenses, ranging from **cyber-dependent crimes** (like hacking and malware distribution) to **cyber-enabled crimes** (such as online fraud and the exploitation of minors).

• **Implementation Agency:** The **United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC)**, which is headquartered in **Vienna**, **Austria**, serves as the secretariat for the convention and will play a lead role in its implementation and **global monitoring**.

questions.question: A computer performs millions of calculations in a fraction of a second. Which characteristic is primarily demonstrated here?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Speed**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Speed** is the most prominent characteristic of a computer, as it can process **millions of instructions** in a **fraction of a second**. This allows for complex **mathematical calculations** and **data processing** tasks that would take humans years to complete.
 
• The **speed** of a computer is measured in different units depending on the type of system; for **microcomputers**, it is typically measured in **Gigahertz (GHz)**, representing billions of **clock cycles per second**.
 
• For high-performance systems and **supercomputers**, **speed** is often measured in **MIPS (Millions of Instructions Per Second)** or **FLOPS (Floating Point Operations Per Second)**, which tracks how many **decimal calculations** can be handled simultaneously.
 
• A computer performs operations at the level of **microseconds (10⁻⁶)**, **nanoseconds (10⁻⁹)**, and even **picoseconds (10⁻¹²)**, making it indispensable for **real-time applications** such as **satellite launching** and **stock market trading**.
 
• The **functions** of the **Central Processing Unit (CPU)** are designed to minimize **latency**, ensuring that the **execution time** for **binary logic gates** is kept to an absolute minimum.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Accuracy**: This refers to the **precision** of the computer's results. If the **input data** is correct, the computer will produce **100% accurate** results. Errors are usually caused by humans (incorrect **algorithms** or data), a phenomenon known as **GIGO (Garbage In, Garbage Out)**.
 
• **Versatility**: A computer is a **versatile** machine capable of performing almost any **task** provided it can be reduced to a **series of logical steps**. It can be used for **scientific research**, **graphic design**, **financial accounting**, and **entertainment** without changing its **hardware** structure.
 
• **Storage (Memory)**: Computers have a massive **storage capacity**. They use **Primary Memory (RAM)** for active tasks and **Secondary Storage** like **Hard Disk Drives (HDD)** or **Solid State Drives (SSD)** for permanent retention. Data is measured in **Bytes**, **Kilobytes (KB)**, **Megabytes (MB)**, **Gigabytes (GB)**, and **Terabytes (TB)**.
 
• **Diligence**: Unlike humans, computers do not suffer from **tiredness**, **boredom**, or **lack of concentration**. They can work **24/7** for **days** or **months** while maintaining the exact same **speed** and **accuracy** for every **instruction**.
 
• **No I.Q.**: A computer lacks an **Intelligence Quotient**; it cannot think or make **decisions** on its own. It relies entirely on the **software** and **instructions** provided by the **user** or **programmer**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Evolution of Speed**: In **1965**, **Gordon Moore** predicted that the number of **transistors** on a **microchip** would double approximately every **two years**, a principle known as **Moore's Law**, which has driven the exponential growth in **processing speed**.
 
• **Microprocessors**: The transition from **vacuum tubes** to **transistors** and later to **Integrated Circuits (ICs)** significantly enhanced the **speed** and reduced the **size** of computers. Modern **multi-core processors** allow **parallel processing**, further boosting **efficiency**.
 
• **Applications**: The **speed** characteristic is critical in **weather forecasting**, where **supercomputers** analyze **atmospheric data** in **real-time** to predict **cyclones** or **rainfall**.
 
• **Data Transfer Speed**: Apart from **processing speed**, computers also feature high **I/O (Input/Output) speed**, often measured in **bits per second (bps)** or **Megabits per second (Mbps)**, which is vital for **internet connectivity** and **network communications**.

__
 
• The procedure for the **impeachment** of the **President of India** is a **quasi-judicial procedure** explicitly mentioned in **Article 61** of the **Constitution of India**.
 
• The **charge** for the impeachment of the **President** can be **preferred** by **either House of the Parliament**, which means it can originate in either the **Lok Sabha** or the **Rajya Sabha**.
 
• To initiate the process, the **charges** must be **signed** by at least **one-fourth (1/4th)** of the **total membership** of the **House** that framed the charges.
 
• A **14 days prior notice** in writing must be given to the **President** before the resolution is moved in the House.
 
• The **resolution** to impeach the **President** must be **passed** by a **majority** of **not less than two-thirds (2/3rd)** of the **total membership** of the **House** in which it was introduced.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Grounds for Impeachment**:

 
 
• The only **ground** for the **impeachment** of the **President** mentioned in the **Constitution** is the **"Violation of the Constitution"**. However, the term "Violation of the Constitution" is **not defined** in the **Constitution of India**.
 
 
 
• **Investigation by the Second House**:
 
 
• After the **resolution** is **passed** by the **originating House**, it is **sent** to the **other House**, which **investigates** the **charges** or causes the charges to be investigated.
 
• During this **investigation**, the **President** has the **right to appear** and to be **represented** to defend themselves.
 
• If the **second House** also **sustains** the **charge** and **passes** the **impeachment resolution** with a **majority** of **not less than two-thirds (2/3rd)** of the **total membership**, the **President** stands **removed** from **office** from the **date** on which the resolution is so passed.
 
 
 
• **Participation in Impeachment**:
 
 
• The **nominated members** of **either House of Parliament** **can participate** in the **impeachment** of the **President**, even though they **do not participate** in the **election** of the **President**.
 
• The **elected members** of the **Legislative Assemblies** of **States** and the **Union Territories** of **Delhi** and **Puducherry** **do not participate** in the **impeachment** process, even though they **participate** in the **Presidential election**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**:
 
 
• To date, **no President of India** has ever been **impeached**.
 
• The **President** serves a **term** of **five years** from the date of entering office, as per **Article 56**, but can be **removed** earlier through this process.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 56(1)(b)**: States that the **President** may, for **violation of the Constitution**, be removed from office by **impeachment** in the manner provided in **Article 61**.
 
• **Vacancy in Office**: If the **office** of the **President** falls **vacant** due to **impeachment**, **resignation**, or **death**, an **election** to fill the vacancy must be held **within six months**.
 
• **Executive Powers**: While the **impeachment** is a **legislative check**, the **President** remains the **nominal head** and the **Supreme Commander** of the **Defence Forces** of **India** until the resolution is successfully passed.

• When this **shortcut** is used while the **Desktop** is in focus (meaning no specific application window is active), it opens the **Windows Shut Down** dialog. This **feature** allows users to quickly **Shut Down**, **Restart**, **Sleep**, or **Sign Out** of the **system** without using the **Start Menu**.
 
• The **ALT + F4** command sends a specific **signal** known as **WM_CLOSE** to the **software**. This is a "polite" way to close a program, as it allows the **application** to perform **cleanup tasks** or prompt for file saving

questions.question: The sum of the cubes of the numbers 55, –30 and –25 is equal to:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use identity: a + b + c = 0 ⇒ a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc

⇒ 55 − 30 − 25 = 0

⇒ So sum = 3 × 55 × (−30) × (−25)

⇒ = 3 × 55 × 750 = 123750

**∴ Answer = 123750**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Numbers = 55, −30, −25

**Concept Used:**

a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca)

**Calculation:**

⇒ a + b + c = 55 − 30 − 25 = 0

⇒ So, a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc

⇒ = 3 × 55 × (−30) × (−25)

⇒ = 3 × 55 × 750

⇒ = 123750

**∴ Sum of cubes = 123750**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Special Identity:** If a + b + c = 0 ⇒ a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc

**General Identity:** a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(...)

**Shortcut Tip:** Always check if sum is zero before expanding cubes

**Sign Rule:** Negative × Negative = Positive

questions.question: When the kidneys are not able to reabsorb the glucose, then the glucose will be excreted through the urine. This condition is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Glycosuria**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Glycosuria** is a medical condition characterized by the excretion of **glucose** in the urine. Under normal physiological conditions, the **kidneys** filter **glucose** through the **glomerulus** and then reabsorb nearly **100%** of it back into the **bloodstream**.
 
• The reabsorption process primarily takes place in the **Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT)** of the **nephron**. This is facilitated by specialized transport proteins known as **Sodium-Glucose Co-transporters (SGLT1 and SGLT2)**. *Hence, the definition matches the condition described in the question.*
 
• There is a limit to how much **glucose** the **kidneys** can reabsorb, known as the **Renal Threshold**. For most healthy adults, this threshold is approximately **160 to 180 mg/dL** of **blood glucose**.
 
• When **blood sugar levels** exceed this threshold, the **SGLT** transporters become saturated (reach their maximum capacity), and the excess **glucose** is spilled into the urine.
 
• The most common cause of **Glycosuria** is **Diabetes Mellitus** (Type 1 or Type 2), where high levels of **blood glucose** result in significant sugar loss through the **urinary system**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ascites**: This refers to the abnormal buildup of **fluid** in the **peritoneal cavity** (abdomen). It is frequently caused by **Liver Cirrhosis**, **portal hypertension**, or **heart failure**. It is not related to the excretion of glucose.
 
• **Lupus Nephritis**: This is an **autoimmune disease** that occurs as a complication of **Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE)**. In this condition, the body's immune system attacks the **kidneys**, specifically the **glomeruli**, leading to **proteinuria** (protein in urine) or **hematuria** (blood in urine), but not specifically primary glycosuria.
 
• **Cystinosis**: This is a rare **lysosomal storage disorder** caused by **genetic mutations**. It leads to the accumulation of **cystine crystals** in various organs, especially the **kidneys**. This can lead to **Fanconi Syndrome**, where the **kidneys** fail to reabsorb various substances like **glucose**, **amino acids**, and **electrolytes**.
 
• **Renal Glycosuria**: Unlike diabetic glycosuria, **Renal Glycosuria** is a rare condition where **glucose** is excreted in the urine despite **normal blood sugar levels**. This happens due to a specific functional defect in the **renal tubules**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Diagnosis**: **Glycosuria** is usually detected during a **Urinalysis** using a **dipstick test**. The presence of sugar is indicated by a color change on the chemically treated strip.
 
• **Symptoms**: While **Glycosuria** itself might be asymptomatic, the underlying **Diabetes Mellitus** often causes **Polyuria** (excessive urination), **Polydipsia** (excessive thirst), and **Polyphagia** (excessive hunger).
 
• **Gestational Glycosuria**: It is common for **pregnant women** to exhibit **Glycosuria** because the **Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR)** increases during **pregnancy**, and the **Renal Threshold** for glucose may naturally decrease.
 
• **Historical Context**: The term comes from the Greek words "glykys" (sweet) and "ouron" (urine). Ancient physicians used to diagnose the "honey-sweet" urine of diabetics by observing if **ants** were attracted to it.

(34, 1088, 16)

(21, 420, 10)
